records.subject: Getting started with Wrenfield
records.body:
Hi Leo,

Welcome aboard! Wrenfield is built for teams, so it gets more useful once at least one other person is in it -- a teammate can be invited from Account Settings -> Members at any time.

Happy to help if you hit a wall.

Best,
Nadia Goldberg

decisions.rationale: Six days in with no first project, no invite, no tickets, and zero customer replies to either outreach (email:5d59a91a, email:76d4eeae). Total silence plus three stall reasons makes unaided activation in the remaining 8 days unlikely, though an active paid Team plan leaves some chance of self-start.

draft.subject: A quick hand getting Timber Group's first project up
draft.body:
Hi Leo,

No reply needed to my last note — I know new tools can slip down the list in a first week.

In Wrenfield, projects are the main organizing unit, and tasks live inside them, and the in-app onboarding flow walks through creating a first project. Wrenfield also gets more useful once someone else is in it — a teammate can be invited from Account Settings -> Members at any time, and teammates can be bulk-invited from a CSV file instead of one at a time.

Would a 15-minute call this week help? I'll walk through that first project with you and answer anything that comes up.

Best,
Nadia
